name: ERNC27
title: ERN Conference 2027
theme: Think & Do: Where Research, Competition & Community Converge
intro:
Esports has always lived in three worlds at once, especially in education. It is a field of research that has produced its own handbooks, journals, and degree programs in little more than a decade; it is a competitive practice that spans from the scholastic leagues to world championships; and it is a community of players, fans, organizers, clubs, universities, and cities. These three worlds, however, meet less often than they should.

NC State’s motto, Think & Do, describes the task ERNC27 sets itself. We invite contributions that think about esports, contributions that do something with it, and, above all, those that do both. Three questions run through the conference:

- What can research learn from esports competition and community, and what does it owe them in return?
- How do esports competitive structures, from collegiate programs to professional circuits, shape the communities around them?
- When esports research, competition, and community converge, what makes that convergence last?

name: ERNC26
theme: Bridging Gaming Heritage and Esports Futures: Transformations, Traditions, and Tomorrow
summary:
### Conference Overview

The Esports Research Network Conference 2026 (ERNC26) took place from **15 to 17 September 2026** at the **University of Tsukuba**, in the University's 30th Anniversary Hall (Daigaku Kaikan). After the fully online edition of 2025, ERNC26 brought the network back into one room, and it did so in a country that shaped the history of games like few others. Japan is a gaming powerhouse with an unparalleled heritage in console and arcade gaming; its esports ecosystem, however, has only recently started to grow, helped by the relaxation of prize money regulations in 2018 and the rise of professional leagues. Consequently, Tsukuba was a fitting place to ask what gaming heritage means for the future of esports.

The conference was hosted by the University of Tsukuba, funded by the KDDI Foundation and the Tsukuba Tourism and Convention Association, and co-organized by GAKU.

### Theme and Contributions

ERNC26 was organized under the theme **“Bridging Gaming Heritage and Esports Futures: Transformations, Traditions, and Tomorrow”**, with a particular focus on intercultural perspectives and on the relationship between Asia and other regions. The program reflected the breadth of the field. Health and performance science was strongly represented, from physical conditioning and cardiovascular reactivity to exercise adherence and the menstrual cycle in training and competition. Governance and integrity formed a second cluster, with work on legal frameworks, e-doping, AI ethics and the role of the state. Further sessions examined fandom across borders, collegiate esports, inclusion, older adults as players, and esports tourism.

Three keynotes framed the program: **Hideki Okamura** (SEGA, JESU and GAKU) on the esports journey in Japan, **Brian McCauley** (Jönköping International Business School) on gaming heritage as infrastructure for esports and the digital society, and **Michael Murray** (Bandai Namco Entertainment) on keeping community at the heart of esports. An opening panel with SEGA, KONAMI Esports Academy and the Japan Esports Union discussed how publishers and public authorities shape Japan's esports scene.

### Format and Participation

ERNC26 brought together **163 participants from 29 countries** and more than 40 institutions. The Book of Abstracts contains **64 peer-reviewed presentations and one panel**, held in four parallel session rooms alongside the keynotes and industry panels. In line with ERN practice, the plenary sessions were streamed on the ERN Twitch channel and the recordings are published on the ERN YouTube channel.

### Media and Documentation

Recordings of the sessions and the pre-recorded online presentations are available on the ERN YouTube channel.

name: ERNC25
theme: Future Realities: Esports as a Global Lab
summary:
The Esports Research Network Conference 2025 (ERNC 2025) was held from 12 to 14 November 2025 as a fully online, global conference. Building on previous editions, ERNC25 brought together researchers, practitioners, and students from around the world through a continuous, live digital format designed to support sustained international exchange.

The conference was structured around a hub-based production model, with four regional hubs operating as research and live-streaming nodes. These hubs were hosted by Slippery Rock University of Pennsylvania and Michigan State University (Americas), Staffordshire University (Europe, Middle East and Africa), and UNSW Sydney (Asia-Pacific). Together, the hubs enabled ERNC25 to follow the sun across time zones and remain continuously live throughout the three-day conference.

ERNC 2025 was organized under the theme “Future Realities: Esports as a Global Lab”, positioning esports as both an object of study and a methodological lens for understanding digital transformation.

name: ERNC24
summary:
The Esports Research Network Conference 2024 (ERNC 2024) was held from 30 October to 1 November 2024 in London, United Kingdom. ERNC24 once again brought together an international community of researchers, industry professionals, and practitioners to explore critical questions at the intersection of esports, society, and digital culture. The conference was held in a hybrid format, combining in-person participation with online access.

Taking place in the lead-up to the League of Legends World Finals in London, ERNC24 situated esports research within a broader cultural and economic moment, highlighting the growing entanglement of competitive gaming with global media, sport, and urban environments.

ERNC 2024 was organized under the theme “Where Worlds Collide”, capturing the growing intersections between esports and traditional sport, culture, media, technology, education, and governance.
facts: Tom Brock, Manchester Metropolitan University, and Cameron Vanloo, Staffordshire University, United Kingdom

Brett Abarbanel, “The Bettor Part of Valor(ant)”; Emma Witkowski, “Collisions, Context & Coming Together: Exploring the Intersection of Traditional Sports & Esports”; Anna Baumann, “Beyond the Agora: Esports and the Fractured Dream of a Unified Society”
Diversity and inclusion, ethical challenges, sustainable business in esports, careers and HR, education, and research development

name: ERNC22
theme: Sustainable Esports in the Digital Society
summary:
The Esports Research Network Conference 2022 (ERNC 2022) was held as an international in-person conference from 21 to 23 November 2022 in Jönköping, Sweden, and was presented by the Media, Management & Transformation Centre (MMTC) at Jönköping International Business School. ERNC 2022 marked the first fully in-person ERN conference and brought together researchers, students, practitioners, and industry stakeholders to engage with pressing questions surrounding sustainability in esports and the digital society.

Hosted in Jönköping, widely recognized as the City of DreamHack, the conference was strategically aligned with DreamHack Winter 2022 (24 to 27 November), enabling participants to connect academic debate with one of the world’s largest digital and esports festivals. Selected key sessions and panels were live-streamed to ensure broader accessibility and international reach.

ERNC 2022 focused on Sustainable Esports in the Digital Society, addressing how esports can continue to develop while maintaining long-term economic viability, social responsibility, and environmental awareness.

name: ERNC21
summary:
The first Esports Research Network Conference (ERNC 2021) was hosted by the Esports Research Network in collaboration with the Institut des Sciences du Sport-Santé (I3SP) at the University of Paris. The conference took place online on 9 and 10 December 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic and brought together an international and multidisciplinary community of researchers, students, and industry professionals.

ERNC 2021 focused on Esports Health and Well-being Management, addressing physical, mental, and social dimensions of health within competitive gaming. The conference positioned esports as both a high-performance environment and a lens through which broader questions of health, wellbeing, and sustainability in digital society can be examined.
facts: Nicolas Besombes, University of Paris, France
104 authors and speakers, 638 registered attendees and more than 2,300 unique viewers
